a≡r (mod q),  a≡−1 (mod d).

x^{n−1}=x^{φ(n)}≡1 (mod q).

Thus d∣n−1. But n≡−1 (mod d), so d∣2, contradicting d>2. Therefore d≤2, and hence x^2≡1 (mod q).

There are infinitely many primes q≡1 (mod 4) not dividing y. Indeed, if q_1,…,q_k were all of them, set A=2yq_1⋯q_k and take a prime divisor q of A^2+1. Then q∤A, and A has order 4 modulo q, so q≡1 (mod 4), producing a new such prime.
